title: GOD SEES THE HEART BEHIND THE GIFT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not bring anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted
on your behalf. When anyone brings from the herd or flock a fellowship
offering to the LORD to fulfill a special vow or as a freewill
offering, it must be without defect or blemish to be acceptable'"
- Lev 22:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The word that stands out is "acceptable." God was not simply collecting
livestock. He was receiving worship, and He looked past the animal to
the heart that brought it.

Centuries later, the prophet Malachi confronted Israel for offering
blind and crippled animals, asking whether they would dare present such
a gift to their governor (Mal 1:8). The animals were only a symptom.
The real problem was a heart that had stopped caring.

Dear friend, God still looks past the outward act. He sees the couple
who give quietly and sacrificially. He sees the widow with two small
coins and calls it more than all the rest (Mark 12:43-44). He also sees
the impressive gift given for applause.

This should encourage anyone who feels they have little to offer. God
is not measuring the size. He is looking at the heart. Paul says each
should give what they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly or
under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7).

The gift that pleases God is not the biggest one. It is the honest one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I give to God, what is actually going on in my heart?
2. Do I give cheerfully or reluctantly?
3. Am I more concerned with how my giving looks than with what it
   means?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see my heart behind everything I bring You. Purify my
motives and make my giving joyful rather than grudging. Amen.
